Chapter 202

Anticholinergics

Tintinalli Ch.202 + Rosen Ch.140 — Antimuscarinic Toxidrome, Physostigmine, Diphenhydramine

Frank LoVecchio; Rosen: Jason A. Hoppe and Andrew A. Monte

Thai EM BoardTintinalliRosen'sToxicology chapter

Introduction: Anticholinergic Exposures

Fast Frame

Anticholinergic ในบทนี้ควรคิดเป็น antimuscarinic toxidrome: ยับยั้ง muscarinic receptor ทั้งใน CNS และ peripheral nervous system.

Most common overdose: diphenhydramine.

Classic natural alkaloids: atropine, hyoscyamine, scopolamine.

High-risk groups: children, elderly/polypharmacy, adolescents using Datura/belladonna plants.

Delayed presentations: decreased GI motility can prolong absorption; diphenoxylate-atropine may present late.

Pharmacology: Why The Toxidrome Looks This Way

Mechanism in One Screen

Muscarinic blockade removes parasympathetic effects. ผลคือ dry secretions, mydriasis, tachycardia, ileus, urinary retention, delirium.

Important wording: “anticholinergic” ใช้ทั่วไป แต่ toxic effect หลักในบทนี้คือ antimuscarinic. Nicotinic neuromuscular blockade ไม่ใช่ feature หลักของ toxidrome นี้.

Board pearl M2 blockade ที่ SA node = tachycardia; M3 blockade ที่ sweat gland = anhidrosis และ hyperthermia.

Clinical Features: Recognize It Fast

Dry as a bonedry mouth, dry axilla, ↓ sweating
Red as a beetflushed warm skin
Hot as hadeshyperthermia from anhidrosis + agitation
Blind as a batmydriasis, blurred vision
Mad as a hatterdelirium, hallucination, mumbling speech
Full as a flaskurinary retention

Tintinalli source check

Table 202-3. Muscarinic vs Antimuscarinic Effects

ใช้แยก feature เป็น organ system. จุดสอบ: dry skin/axilla แยกจาก sympathomimetic ที่มัก sweaty.

Do Not Miss

Diphenhydramine/TCA-like co-toxicity อาจมี wide QRS / QT prolongation / ventricular dysrhythmia / seizures. Pure antimuscarinic toxicity โดยทั่วไปไม่ควรมี QRS widening.

Differential Diagnosis: Anticholinergic vs Look-Alikes

Anticholinergic

Hot, dry, flushed, mydriatic, delirious. Bowel sounds ↓, urinary retention, dry axilla.

Sympathomimetic

Agitated + tachy + mydriasis แต่ skin มัก sweaty; bowel sounds not classically absent.

Serotonin Syndrome

Clonus, hyperreflexia, diaphoresis. Neuromuscular findings ช่วยแยก.

NMS

Lead-pipe rigidity, fever, altered mental status, autonomic instability; evolves slower.

Rosen source check

Box 140.2. Differential Considerations

Rosen ย้ำ differential broad ทั้ง toxicologic, CNS, metabolic และ psychiatric causes. อย่าให้ “delirium + tachycardia” พาเราไป physostigmine เร็วเกินถ้า toxidrome ไม่ครบ.

Diagnosis: Pattern First, ECG Always

Diagnostic Checklist

  • Glucose for any altered mental status.
  • ECG to detect sodium-channel blockade: QRS widening, terminal R in aVR, QT prolongation.
  • CK/electrolytes/renal function if hyperthermia, agitation, or rhabdomyolysis risk.
  • Drug screens rarely confirm anticholinergic agents; false positives for cyclic antidepressants can occur with diphenhydramine/hydroxyzine.

Before Physostigmine

ต้องดู ECG ก่อน. Do not give physostigmine if TCA/sodium-channel blockade suspected, QRS >120 ms, bradycardia, AV block, or seizure from current overdose.

Management: Support, Cool, Sedate, Reverse Selectively

Tintinalli source check

Table 202-4. Treatment of Anticholinergic Toxicity

Table นี้คือ management spine: charcoal, benzodiazepines, sodium bicarbonate, physostigmine.

1. ABC + monitoringcontinuous cardiac monitoring, temperature, glucose, IV access.
2. Decontaminationactivated charcoal only early and airway protected; decreased GI motility may prolong absorption.
3. Sedate safelybenzodiazepines for agitation/seizures; avoid antipsychotics when possible.
4. Cool aggressivelyexternal cooling, fluids, treat rhabdomyolysis; antipyretics do not fix anhidrosis.
5. Treat wide QRSsodium bicarbonate if sodium-channel blockade/wide-complex tachydysrhythmia.
6. Physostigminefor severe antimuscarinic delirium when ECG and history are appropriate.

Plant-Based Anticholinergic Poisoning

Plants to Remember

Datura, Atropa belladonna, Hyoscyamus, Mandragora, and Brugmansia can produce classic toxidrome. Onset often 1-4 hours after ingestion and sooner if smoked/inhaled.

Rosen source check

Table 140.1. Specific Agents and Unique Manifestations

Rosen adds agent-specific risk: Datura seed dose, diphenhydramine/TCA sodium-channel effects, doxylamine rhabdomyolysis, atypical antipsychotic mixed receptor effects.

Key Points: Anticholinergic Poisoning

Pattern

Hot, dry, flushed, blind, mad, full. Dry axilla + urinary retention are high-yield clues.

Differentiate

Sympathomimetic = sweaty. Serotonin = clonus/hyperreflexia. Cholinergic = SLUDGE/bronchorrhea/miosis.

ECG First

Check QRS/QTc/aVR before physostigmine. Wide QRS changes management.

Agitation

Benzodiazepines are safe first-line sedation and reduce heat generation.

Hyperthermia

เกิดจาก anhidrosis + agitation. Cool externally; antipyretics are not the answer.

Physostigmine

Best for severe pure antimuscarinic delirium when ECG is safe. Watch for cholinergic excess.

Diphenhydramine

Commonest cause; large overdoses can cause seizure, QRS widening, QT prolongation.

Disposition

Mild resolved cases observe; severe delirium, hyperthermia, ECG abnormality, seizure, or physostigmine need monitored setting.

Inline Assessment MCQs

Q1. A 22-year-old presents with agitation, confusion, mumbling speech, picking at imaginary objects, hot dry flushed skin, HR 140, and mydriasis. Temperature is 38.4°C. He is unable to void. Which toxidrome does this presentation represent?
  • A. Cholinergic toxidrome from organophosphate poisoning
  • B. Sympathomimetic toxidrome from stimulant abuse
  • C. Anticholinergic toxidrome from muscarinic receptor blockade
  • D. Serotonin syndrome from SSRI toxicity
❌ Incorrect. Cholinergic toxidrome presents with miosis, SLUDGE (salivation, lacrimation, urination, defecation, GI emesis), bronchospasm, and bradycardia — the opposite of this presentation.
❌ Incorrect. Sympathomimetic toxidrome (cocaine, methamphetamine) also has mydriasis, tachycardia, and hyperthermia, but skin is typically diaphoretic (sweating) — not hot and dry. Agitation is present in both.
✅ Correct. Hot, dry, flushed skin (anhidrosis) is the key distinguishing feature from sympathomimetic toxidrome. Mydriasis, tachycardia, urinary retention, and delirium complete the anticholinergic picture.
❌ Incorrect. Serotonin syndrome has agitation, hyperthermia, and autonomic instability, but presents with clonus, hyperreflexia, and diaphoresis (not dry skin). Mydriasis may occur in both.
Q2. A 68-year-old woman is brought from a nursing home with delirium. Her medications include oxybutynin, diphenhydramine, amitriptyline, and metformin. Examination shows dry mucous membranes, HR 118, temperature 38.1°C, and urinary retention. Which medication is most likely responsible?
  • A. Metformin
  • B. Amitriptyline (TCA)
  • C. Metformin combined with oxybutynin
  • D. Oxybutynin alone
❌ Incorrect. Metformin (biguanide antidiabetic) has no anticholinergic properties. It should not cause this presentation.
✅ Correct. Amitriptyline has one of the highest anticholinergic potencies among prescription medications. Combined with oxybutynin and diphenhydramine, her cumulative anticholinergic burden is very high. TCAs also carry risk of cardiac toxicity (QRS prolongation, arrhythmias).
❌ Incorrect. Metformin has no anticholinergic activity. Oxybutynin does have anticholinergic effects but amitriptyline is the most potent contributor.
❌ Incorrect. Oxybutynin is an anticholinergic agent, but amitriptyline has a much higher anticholinergic burden and is more likely to cause significant toxicity. The combination matters, but amitriptyline is the most dangerous.

Thai EM Board MCQs

Q1. ผู้ป่วยหญิงอายุ 19 ปี ถูกส่งมาด้วยอาการประสาทหลอน ปากแห้ง ผิวแดง ตาพร่า และ HR 155 ครั้ง/นาที ญาติเล่าว่าผู้ป่วยไปเที่ยวงาน festival มาก่อนหน้านี้ ตาโต ECG พบ QRS 95 ms ข้อใดต่อไปนี้เป็นการรักษาเฉพาะที่เหมาะสมที่สุด?
  • A. Atropine IV เพื่อ control tachycardia
  • B. Physostigmine 1-2 mg IV ช้าๆ เพื่อ reverse anticholinergic toxidrome
  • C. Sodium bicarbonate IV เพื่อ alkalinize serum
  • D. Benzodiazepine IV เพื่อแก้ agitation แต่ไม่ใช้ physostigmine
❌ ผิด. Atropine เป็น anticholinergic — จะทำให้อาการแย่ลงมาก ห้ามใช้ใน anticholinergic toxidrome
✅ ถูก. Physostigmine เป็น antidote สำหรับ anticholinergic toxidrome โดย inhibit acetylcholinesterase ทำให้ ACh เพิ่มขึ้นเอาชนะ anticholinergic blockade ข้ามผ่าน BBB ได้ แก้ delirium และ peripheral symptoms QRS ปกติช่วยยืนยันไม่ใช่ TCA
❌ ผิด. Sodium bicarbonate ใช้สำหรับ TCA overdose ที่ทำให้ QRS กว้าง (>120 ms) QRS ปกติในผู้ป่วยรายนี้ไม่ใช่ข้อบ่งชี้
❌ ผิด. Benzodiazepine ช่วยได้สำหรับ agitation แต่ physostigmine เป็น definitive antidote ที่ reverse ทั้ง peripheral และ central symptoms โดยตรง
Q2. ผู้ป่วยชายอายุ 45 ปี มีประวัติ depression กินยา amitriptyline 1500 mg ถูกส่งมาด้วยอาการซึม ตาโต ปากแห้ง HR 130 ECG พบ QRS 145 ms และ QTc 520 ms ข้อใดต่อไปนี้ควรหลีกเลี่ยงโดยเด็ดขาดในผู้ป่วยรายนี้?
  • A. Sodium bicarbonate 1-2 mEq/kg IV bolus
  • B. Benzodiazepine สำหรับ seizure prophylaxis
  • C. Physostigmine 2 mg IV
  • D. Intralipid emulsion 20% IV
❌ ผิด (เหมาะสม). Sodium bicarbonate เป็น first-line สำหรับ TCA-induced QRS widening — alkalinization เอาชนะ sodium channel blockade ของ TCA
❌ ผิด (เหมาะสม). Benzodiazepines เป็น first-line สำหรับ TCA-induced seizures — ห้ามใช้ phenytoin
✅ ถูก (ต้องหลีกเลี่ยง). Physostigmine เป็น contraindicated ใน TCA overdose เพราะอาจทำให้เกิด bradycardia, heart block, และ asystole ในผู้ป่วยที่มี sodium channel blockade จาก TCA
❌ ผิด (อาจพิจารณาได้). Intralipid ใช้ได้สำหรับ refractory TCA toxicity (lipid sink therapy) — ไม่ใช่ contraindicated
Q3. ผู้ป่วยเด็กอายุ 4 ปี กินเมล็ดต้น Jimsonweed (Datura) ที่พบในสวน ถูกส่งมาด้วยอาการตื่นเต้น ประสาทหลอน ตาโต และผิวหน้าแดง อุณหภูมิ 38.5°C HR 155 ครั้ง/นาที ข้อใดเป็น mechanism ที่ถูกต้องของพืชชนิดนี้?
  • A. Competitive antagonism ที่ muscarinic receptor จาก atropine, scopolamine, hyoscyamine
  • B. Cholinesterase inhibition คล้าย organophosphate
  • C. Serotonin reuptake inhibition ทำให้เกิด serotonin syndrome
  • D. Alpha-adrenergic stimulation ทำให้เกิด sympathomimetic toxidrome
✅ ถูก. Datura มี tropane alkaloids ที่ block muscarinic receptors อย่าง competitive ทำให้เกิด anticholinergic toxidrome ครบถ้วน
❌ ผิด. Datura ไม่ inhibit cholinesterase แต่ block muscarinic receptor โดยตรง อาการจึงตรงข้ามกับ organophosphate poisoning
❌ ผิด. Datura ไม่มีผลต่อ serotonin system อาการเป็น anticholinergic ไม่ใช่ serotonin syndrome
❌ ผิด. Datura ไม่กระตุ้น alpha-adrenergic receptor อาการแยกจาก sympathomimetic ได้จาก hot dry skin (ไม่ใช่ diaphoresis)
Q4. ผู้ป่วยได้รับ physostigmine 1.5 mg IV แก้ anticholinergic toxidrome จาก Datura สำเร็จ แต่ 45 นาทีต่อมาอาการ delirium กลับมาอีก ข้อใดอธิบายเหตุการณ์นี้ได้ดีที่สุดและควรจัดการอย่างไร?
  • A. ผู้ป่วยเกิด physostigmine toxicity แสดงว่า dose เกิน ต้องหยุดยา
  • B. Physostigmine หมดฤทธิ์ก่อน alkaloid — ให้ physostigmine ซ้ำหรือ continuous infusion
  • C. ผู้ป่วยมี co-ingestion ของ stimulant — ส่ง urine drug screen
  • D. ผู้ป่วย refractory ต่อ physostigmine — เปลี่ยนเป็น benzodiazepine เท่านั้น
❌ ผิด. อาการ delirium กลับมาไม่ใช่ physostigmine toxicity (ซึ่งจะเป็น cholinergic crisis: น้ำลาย, bradycardia, seizure) แต่เป็น recurrence เพราะ physostigmine หมดฤทธิ์
✅ ถูก. Physostigmine half-life ~20-45 นาที สั้นกว่า Datura alkaloids มาก Recurrence จึงเป็นเรื่องที่คาดได้ การให้ซ้ำหรือ infusion แก้ปัญหานี้ได้
❌ ผิด. Recurrence ตามเวลาที่สอดคล้องกับ physostigmine half-life บ่งชี้ pharmacokinetic mismatch ระหว่าง antidote และ toxin ไม่ใช่ co-ingestion
❌ ผิด. ผู้ป่วยตอบสนองต่อ physostigmine ครั้งแรก แสดงว่า Recurrence จาก pharmacokinetics ไม่ใช่ refractory ควรให้ physostigmine ซ้ำ

Thai EM Board — InTraining Exam MCQs

Q1. A 35-year-old male presents with agitation, mumbling speech, and picking behaviors. Physical examination reveals HR 148, temperature 39.2°C, dry flushed skin, urinary retention, and mydriasis 8 mm bilaterally. He was found with empty blister packs of diphenhydramine. His ECG shows QRS 82 ms and QTc 440 ms. Which of the following is the most appropriate specific treatment?
  • A. Haloperidol 5 mg IM for acute agitation management
  • B. Sodium bicarbonate 1-2 mEq/kg IV for cardioprotection
  • C. Physostigmine 1-2 mg IV slow push over 5 minutes with cardiac monitoring
  • D. Diphenhydramine 50 mg IV for antihistamine effect
❌ Incorrect. Haloperidol has anticholinergic properties and may worsen toxicity. It also lowers the seizure threshold and may prolong QTc — all problematic in anticholinergic toxidrome.
❌ Incorrect. Sodium bicarbonate is indicated for TCA-induced sodium channel blockade (QRS >100-120 ms). This patient has a normal QRS, making sodium bicarbonate unnecessary.
✅ Correct. Pure anticholinergic toxidrome (narrow QRS, confirming no TCA) is a clear indication for physostigmine. It reverses both central (delirium, agitation) and peripheral (tachycardia, urinary retention) anticholinergic effects. Cardiac monitoring is required to detect cholinergic bradycardia.
❌ Incorrect. Diphenhydramine IS the causative agent — giving more would worsen toxicity dramatically.

McGraw-Hill Specialty Board Review MCQs

Q1. Which of the following medications has the HIGHEST anticholinergic burden and is most likely to cause delirium in elderly patients?
  • A. Metoprolol (beta-blocker)
  • B. Amitriptyline (tricyclic antidepressant)
  • C. Sertraline (SSRI)
  • D. Lisinopril (ACE inhibitor)
Amitriptyline (TCA) has one of the highest anticholinergic activities of all prescription drugs. In elderly patients, who are particularly sensitive to anticholinergic effects due to decreased cholinergic reserve, amitriptyline poses a high risk of delirium, falls, urinary retention, and constipation. It is on the Beers Criteria list of medications to avoid in elderly patients.
Q2. A 28-year-old presents with anticholinergic toxidrome. The treating physician considers physostigmine but first checks the ECG. Which ECG finding would be a CONTRAINDICATION to physostigmine?
  • A. Sinus tachycardia at 140 bpm
  • B. QTc of 490 ms
  • C. PR interval of 210 ms (first-degree AV block)
  • D. QRS duration of 130 ms
QRS widening (>100-120 ms) suggests TCA toxicity, which is a contraindication to physostigmine. In TCA overdose, physostigmine can cause severe cholinergic crisis — bradycardia, heart block, asystole — in a patient already with sodium channel blockade and cardiac toxicity. The combination is potentially lethal. QTc prolongation alone (without QRS widening) is less concerning for TCA but warrants caution.
Q3. Which of the following features BEST distinguishes sympathomimetic toxidrome from anticholinergic toxidrome?
  • A. Skin moisture: diaphoretic in sympathomimetic, anhidrotic in anticholinergic
  • B. Heart rate: tachycardia in sympathomimetic, bradycardia in anticholinergic
  • C. Pupil size: mydriasis in sympathomimetic, miosis in anticholinergic
  • D. Blood pressure: hypertension in anticholinergic, hypotension in sympathomimetic
Both sympathomimetic and anticholinergic toxidromes share mydriasis, tachycardia, agitation, and hyperthermia. The key distinguishing feature is SKIN MOISTURE: sympathomimetic toxidrome causes diaphoresis (wet skin from stimulated sweat glands), while anticholinergic toxidrome causes anhidrosis (hot, dry skin due to muscarinic blockade of sweat glands). This single finding rapidly differentiates the two.
Q4. A 19-year-old college student is brought to the ED from a party. She is confused, agitated, and flushed. Her friend states she 'took something.' Urine drug screen is negative. Physical examination: HR 135, Temp 39.1°C, hot dry skin, urinary retention, mydriasis 7 mm. The team administers physostigmine 1.5 mg IV over 5 minutes. Within 15 minutes, she becomes markedly diaphoretic, bradycardic (HR 48), and begins to vomit profusely. What is the most appropriate response?
  • A. Administer a second dose of physostigmine to complete reversal of anticholinergic toxidrome
  • B. Administer atropine IV to reverse physostigmine-induced cholinergic excess
  • C. Administer pralidoxime to reactivate cholinesterase
  • D. Perform immediate transcutaneous pacing for bradycardia
These findings represent physostigmine-induced cholinergic excess: bradycardia, diaphoresis, and GI activation (nausea/vomiting). The antidote for physostigmine toxicity is atropine, which reverses the excess cholinergic effects. Dose: 0.5 mg IV for every 1 mg of physostigmine given, or titrated to effect. This is why cardiac monitoring and atropine availability are mandatory before administering physostigmine.

End-of-Chapter Assessment: 20 Questions

Q1. A 25-year-old presents with hot, dry flushed skin, mydriasis, HR 132, and delirium. What is the mnemonic that describes these findings?
  • A. SLUDGE (Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, GI distress, Emesis)
  • B. Dry as a bone, blind as a bat, red as a beet, hot as a pistol, mad as a hatter, full as a flask
  • C. MUDPILES (Methanol, Uremia, DKA, Propylene glycol, INH, Lactic acidosis, Ethylene glycol, Salicylates)
  • D. RSVP (Respirations slow, Sedation, Vomiting, Pupils small)
❌ Incorrect. SLUDGE describes the CHOLINERGIC (muscarinic) toxidrome — the opposite of anticholinergic.
✅ Correct. This mnemonic captures all major anticholinergic features: anhidrosis, mydriasis, cutaneous flushing, hyperthermia, delirium, and urinary retention.
❌ Incorrect. MUDPILES describes causes of high anion gap metabolic acidosis, not a toxidrome.
❌ Incorrect. These describe opioid toxidrome features, not anticholinergic syndrome.
Q2. Which of the following is NOT part of the anticholinergic toxidrome?
  • A. Urinary retention
  • B. Mydriasis
  • C. Diaphoresis (sweating)
  • D. Decreased bowel sounds
❌ Incorrect (IS anticholinergic). Blockade of detrusor muscle muscarinic receptors causes urinary retention — a classic feature.
❌ Incorrect (IS anticholinergic). Blockade of sphincter pupillae muscle causes pupil dilation (mydriasis).
✅ Correct. Diaphoresis is a CHOLINERGIC feature. Anticholinergic toxidrome causes ANHIDROSIS (dry skin), not sweating.
❌ Incorrect (IS anticholinergic). Muscarinic blockade reduces GI motility, causing ileus and decreased bowel sounds.
Q3. Which anticholinergic agent is unique because it crosses the blood-brain barrier and causes prominent CNS effects including delirium and amnesia?
  • A. Ipratropium (inhaled)
  • B. Scopolamine (hyoscine)
  • C. Glycopyrrolate
  • D. Ipratropium combined with albuterol (Combivent)
❌ Incorrect. Ipratropium is a quaternary ammonium compound that does NOT cross the blood-brain barrier, which is why it causes minimal systemic anticholinergic effects when inhaled.
✅ Correct. Scopolamine is a tertiary amine that crosses the BBB readily, causing delirium, hallucinations, and amnesia. It is more sedating and CNS-active than atropine.
❌ Incorrect. Glycopyrrolate is a quaternary ammonium compound that does not cross the BBB. It is used clinically to reduce secretions without central effects.
❌ Incorrect. Both components of Combivent are inhaled and do not cause significant central anticholinergic effects.
Q4. A 3-year-old swallows an unknown number of her grandmother's oxybutynin tablets. She is brought to the ED 1 hour later with tachycardia, flushing, and agitation. Temperature is 39.0°C. Which treatment is MOST important initially?
  • A. Activated charcoal 1 g/kg PO
  • B. Physostigmine 0.5 mg IV immediately
  • C. IV atropine for tachycardia control
  • D. Active cooling measures to address hyperthermia
❌ Incorrect as MOST important. The child is agitated, which is a relative contraindication to oral activated charcoal (aspiration risk). Temperature management is more immediately critical.
❌ Incorrect as MOST important. Physostigmine may be appropriate but requires cardiac monitoring and carries risks. Cooling is the most immediate intervention given the high temperature.
❌ Incorrect. Atropine would worsen all anticholinergic symptoms. It is absolutely contraindicated.
✅ Correct. Hyperthermia from anhidrosis is immediately life-threatening in children. Temperature 39°C can rapidly worsen. External cooling (cool water mist, ice packs to groin/axillae/neck) is the most critical initial intervention.
Q5. Which of the following is a contraindication to physostigmine administration?
  • A. Urinary retention
  • B. Delirium with visual hallucinations
  • C. Active bronchospasm
  • D. QRS 90 ms on ECG
❌ Incorrect. Urinary retention is an anticholinergic SYMPTOM and physostigmine would REVERSE it by increasing bladder detrusor tone.
❌ Incorrect. Central anticholinergic delirium is an INDICATION for physostigmine, not a contraindication.
✅ Correct. Physostigmine increases cholinergic tone and would worsen bronchospasm. Active bronchospasm is a contraindication. Other contraindications: TCA overdose (QRS widening), bowel obstruction, bradycardia.
❌ Incorrect. QRS 90 ms is essentially normal and is not a contraindication. QRS widening (>100-120 ms) suggesting TCA toxicity IS a contraindication.
Q6. A patient receives physostigmine for severe anticholinergic delirium. During administration, continuous ECG monitoring is mandatory. Which complication must the treating physician be prepared to reverse immediately?
  • A. Hypertensive emergency from peripheral vasoconstriction
  • B. Bradycardia or asystole from excess cholinergic cardiac effects
  • C. Ventricular fibrillation from QT prolongation
  • D. Respiratory alkalosis from stimulated breathing drive
❌ Incorrect. Physostigmine does not cause vasoconstriction or hypertensive emergency. The key cardiac risk is bradycardia from excess vagal (cholinergic) tone.
✅ Correct. Physostigmine increases vagal tone via ACh, potentially causing severe bradycardia or asystole. Atropine (antidote: 0.5 mg per 1 mg physostigmine) must be immediately at bedside.
❌ Incorrect. Physostigmine does not typically cause QTc prolongation or VF. Bradycardia from vagotonic effect is the primary cardiac concern.
❌ Incorrect. The key respiratory risk with physostigmine is bronchospasm, not hyperventilation or alkalosis.
Q7. A 72-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is prescribed oxybutynin for overactive bladder. Two days later he presents unable to void with a bladder scan of 600 mL. Which property of oxybutynin caused this complication?
  • A. Muscarinic blockade of detrusor M3 receptors reducing bladder contractility in the setting of pre-existing outflow obstruction
  • B. Alpha-adrenergic stimulation increasing urethral sphincter tone
  • C. Central dopaminergic effects altering voiding reflex
  • D. Inhibition of renal aquaporin channels reducing urine output
✅ Correct. Oxybutynin's anticholinergic effect on bladder M3 receptors reduces detrusor contractility. In men with BPH-related outflow obstruction, this precipitates acute urinary retention. BPH is a relative contraindication to anticholinergic bladder agents.
❌ Incorrect. Oxybutynin has no significant alpha-adrenergic activity. The retention results from reduced detrusor function, not increased sphincter resistance.
❌ Incorrect. Oxybutynin's primary mechanism is peripheral muscarinic antagonism, not central dopaminergic effects.
❌ Incorrect. Oxybutynin does not affect renal tubular function or aquaporin channels. The bladder, not the kidney, is the site of toxicity.
Q8. A 55-year-old woman presents after ingesting Atropa belladonna (deadly nightshade) berries. She has classic anticholinergic syndrome. What are the active alkaloids in this plant?
  • A. Physostigmine and neostigmine
  • B. Nicotine and cotinine
  • C. Colchicine and podophyllotoxin
  • D. Atropine, l-hyoscyamine, and scopolamine
❌ Incorrect. These are cholinesterase inhibitors (used as antidotes), not the toxic alkaloids of belladonna.
❌ Incorrect. Nicotine and cotinine are nicotinic agonists found in tobacco, not in Atropa belladonna.
❌ Incorrect. These are plant toxins (colchicine from Colchicum, podophyllotoxin from Podophyllum) that disrupt cell division, not anticholinergic alkaloids.
✅ Correct. Belladonna contains these three tropane alkaloids, all of which competitively antagonize muscarinic receptors, producing the classic anticholinergic toxidrome.
Q9. A patient with anticholinergic toxidrome from diphenhydramine overdose develops temperature of 41.2°C and is becoming increasingly obtunded. What is the BEST explanation for why hyperthermia is so dangerous in this setting?
  • A. Anhidrosis from muscarinic blockade prevents sweating, eliminating the primary heat dissipation mechanism
  • B. Direct hypothalamic reset raises the temperature set point
  • C. Peripheral vasoconstriction prevents heat radiation from skin
  • D. Increased metabolic rate from uncoupled mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation
✅ Correct. Sweat glands require muscarinic (M3) stimulation for secretion. Anticholinergic blockade prevents sweating entirely, so all metabolic heat (from agitation, tachycardia) accumulates. Without the cooling mechanism, temperature escalates rapidly to dangerous levels.
❌ Incorrect. Anticholinergic hyperthermia is NOT a fever from hypothalamic reset — it is impaired heat dissipation (anhidrosis). NSAIDs and antipyretics that target hypothalamic set point are ineffective; external cooling is required.
❌ Incorrect. Anticholinergic toxidrome causes FLUSHING (cutaneous vasodilation), not vasoconstriction. Flushing is the attempt to dissipate heat via radiation, but without sweating, it is insufficient.
❌ Incorrect. Uncoupled oxidative phosphorylation describes the mechanism of hyperthermia in salicylate poisoning. Anticholinergic hyperthermia results from impaired heat dissipation, not increased heat generation via uncoupling.
Q10. Which of the following medications CANNOT cause anticholinergic toxidrome in overdose?
  • A. Diphenhydramine
  • B. Clozapine
  • C. Oxybutynin
  • D. Metoprolol
❌ Incorrect (CAN cause anticholinergic). Diphenhydramine is a potent muscarinic antagonist — one of the most common causes of anticholinergic toxidrome in overdose.
❌ Incorrect (CAN cause anticholinergic). Clozapine has among the highest antimuscarinic potency of all antipsychotics, causing anticholinergic toxidrome in overdose.
❌ Incorrect (CAN cause anticholinergic). Oxybutynin is specifically a muscarinic antagonist used for overactive bladder. Overdose causes classic anticholinergic toxidrome.
✅ Correct. Metoprolol is a beta-1 adrenergic blocker with no anticholinergic activity. Overdose causes bradycardia and hypotension (beta-blockade), not anticholinergic toxidrome.
Q11. During a poison control consultation, you are asked about a case where a patient ingested a plant from a garden. Which plant contains physostigmine, the natural antidote for anticholinergic poisoning?
  • A. Atropa belladonna (deadly nightshade)
  • B. Physostigma venenosum (Calabar bean)
  • C. Datura stramonium (Jimsonweed)
  • D. Nicotiana tabacum (tobacco)
❌ Incorrect. Belladonna contains atropine, scopolamine, and hyoscyamine — anticholinergic agents, not physostigmine.
✅ Correct. Physostigmine was isolated from the Calabar bean (Physostigma venenosum). This carbamate alkaloid inhibits acetylcholinesterase and reverses anticholinergic toxidrome.
❌ Incorrect. Jimsonweed contains atropine, scopolamine, and hyoscyamine — all anticholinergic. It is a cause of anticholinergic toxidrome, not the source of its antidote.
❌ Incorrect. Tobacco contains nicotine, a nicotinic agonist. It does not contain physostigmine.
Q12. A patient is found with a Fentanyl patch applied to her skin AND has been drinking alcohol. She is drowsy with miosis and RR 8. She also has hot dry skin. Which toxidrome is superimposed on the opioid picture?
  • A. Sympathomimetic toxidrome
  • B. Cholinergic toxidrome
  • C. Anticholinergic toxidrome
  • D. Sedative-hypnotic toxidrome
❌ Incorrect. Sympathomimetic toxidrome causes mydriasis, diaphoresis, and hypertension — not hot dry skin or miosis.
❌ Incorrect. Cholinergic toxidrome causes miosis AND diaphoresis AND bronchospasm and bradycardia — not hot dry skin.
✅ Correct. Hot, dry skin represents anhidrosis from muscarinic blockade — an anticholinergic feature superimposed on the opioid picture. Mixed toxidromes must be recognized so both are treated.
❌ Incorrect. Sedative-hypnotic toxidrome (benzodiazepines, barbiturates) causes CNS depression without specific skin changes. Hot dry skin points to anticholinergic toxidrome.
Q13. A 60-year-old with Parkinson's disease on benztropine (an anticholinergic) accidentally takes a double dose. He develops urinary retention and constipation but is otherwise well. What is the most appropriate management?
  • A. Physostigmine 2 mg IV immediately
  • B. Supportive care: urinary catheterization if needed; hold benztropine dose
  • C. Atropine 0.5 mg IV to counteract the anticholinergic effects
  • D. Activated charcoal via nasogastric tube immediately
❌ Incorrect. Physostigmine is not indicated for mild toxicity without delirium or dangerous hyperthermia. The benefits don't outweigh risks for minor symptoms like urinary retention alone.
✅ Correct. Mild anticholinergic toxicity with urinary retention and constipation without delirium or hyperthermia is managed supportively. Catheterize if retention is symptomatic; withhold the next dose.
❌ Incorrect. Atropine is an anticholinergic agent itself — it would worsen all symptoms. Never use atropine to treat anticholinergic toxidrome.
❌ Incorrect. The patient is alert and the ingestion was benztropine (a double dose, not a massive overdose). Activated charcoal is not indicated for this mild presentation without significant systemic toxicity.
Q14. Which second-generation antihistamine is the LEAST likely to cause anticholinergic toxidrome compared to first-generation agents?
  • A. Diphenhydramine (Benadryl)
  • B. Hydroxyzine (Vistaril)
  • C. Loratadine (Claritin)
  • D. Chlorpheniramine (Chlor-Trimeton)
❌ Incorrect. Diphenhydramine is a first-generation antihistamine with potent anticholinergic activity — one of the most common causes of anticholinergic overdose.
❌ Incorrect. Hydroxyzine is a first-generation antihistamine with significant anticholinergic and sedating properties.
✅ Correct. Loratadine is a second-generation (non-sedating) antihistamine with minimal CNS penetration and minimal anticholinergic activity. It was designed specifically to avoid these side effects.
❌ Incorrect. Chlorpheniramine is a first-generation antihistamine with anticholinergic properties, though less potent than diphenhydramine.
Q15. A patient with anticholinergic toxidrome develops agitation and is at risk of injuring himself or staff. Which is the MOST appropriate sedation agent?
  • A. Haloperidol 5 mg IM
  • B. Benzodiazepine (lorazepam or diazepam) IV
  • C. Physical restraints applied immediately
  • D. Ketamine 1 mg/kg IV for rapid sedation
❌ Incorrect. Haloperidol has anticholinergic properties and may worsen toxidrome. It also lowers seizure threshold and prolongs QTc — both concerning in anticholinergic toxidrome.
✅ Correct. Benzodiazepines are first-line for agitation in anticholinergic toxidrome. They provide sedation without worsening cholinergic blockade or adding anticholinergic effects.
❌ Incorrect. Physical restraints increase agitation, metabolic activity, and heat generation — worsening hyperthermia. They should be minimized or avoided when possible.
❌ Incorrect. Ketamine has sympathomimetic and possibly anticholinergic properties, increasing heart rate and potentially worsening hyperthermia. It is not preferred for anticholinergic toxidrome.
Q16. A patient presents with concurrent features of both opioid toxidrome and anticholinergic toxidrome. Naloxone 0.4 mg IV is given with partial improvement of respiratory depression but continued delirium and hot dry skin. What explains the remaining symptoms?
  • A. Naloxone dose was insufficient — administer 2 mg IV
  • B. Opioid-induced hyperthermia is expected and will resolve spontaneously
  • C. This pattern confirms serotonin syndrome requiring cyproheptadine
  • D. Mixed toxidrome: anticholinergic features (delirium, anhidrosis) persist after opioid reversal because they require separate treatment
❌ Incorrect. The respiratory depression improved with naloxone, suggesting adequate opioid reversal. The remaining symptoms (delirium, hot dry skin) are due to a different mechanism — anticholinergic, not opioid.
❌ Incorrect. Opioids do not cause hyperthermia with hot dry skin — they cause hypothermia. The hot dry skin indicates anticholinergic toxidrome from a co-ingested agent.
❌ Incorrect. Serotonin syndrome presents with diaphoresis, clonus, hyperreflexia — not hot dry skin (anhidrosis). The presentation is consistent with co-existing anticholinergic toxidrome.
✅ Correct. Each toxidrome component requires targeted treatment. Naloxone reverses opioid effects; anticholinergic features (delirium, hot dry skin) require separate management — physostigmine, cooling, benzodiazepines for agitation.
Q17. What is the mechanism by which atropine causes tachycardia?
  • A. Blockade of M2 muscarinic receptors on the SA node removes vagal slowing of heart rate
  • B. Direct beta-1 adrenergic stimulation increases SA node automaticity
  • C. Inhibition of potassium channels prolongs action potential and increases rate
  • D. Calcium channel activation increases myocardial contractility and rate
✅ Correct. SA node muscarinic M2 receptors mediate vagal (parasympathetic) slowing. Atropine blocks these receptors, removing vagal brake and allowing intrinsic cardiac pacemaker rate to increase (tachycardia).
❌ Incorrect. Atropine has no beta-adrenergic activity. The tachycardia is from vagal withdrawal, not sympathetic stimulation.
❌ Incorrect. Atropine does not significantly affect potassium channels. Its cardiac effect is mediated through muscarinic receptor blockade.
❌ Incorrect. Atropine does not activate calcium channels. The chronotropic effect is purely through muscarinic M2 blockade on the SA node.
Q18. An emergency physician considers physostigmine for a 30-year-old with delirium. The ECG shows QRS 88 ms and normal axis. The patient is on no known medications. Urine drug screen is negative. Which additional finding would MOST support using physostigmine?
  • A. A serum alcohol level of 200 mg/dL
  • B. Diaphoresis and muscle rigidity on examination
  • C. Hot, dry skin confirmed on full skin exam
  • D. Pinpoint pupils (miosis)
❌ Incorrect. Elevated alcohol level could explain delirium through intoxication, reducing the likelihood that anticholinergic toxidrome is the primary cause requiring physostigmine.
❌ Incorrect. Diaphoresis and rigidity suggest serotonin syndrome or NMS — not anticholinergic toxidrome. These findings argue against physostigmine.
✅ Correct. Hot, dry skin (anhidrosis from muscarinic blockade of sweat glands) is the most specific physical finding for anticholinergic toxidrome. Its presence strongly supports physostigmine as the appropriate antidote.
❌ Incorrect. Miosis is characteristic of opioid or cholinergic toxidrome — the opposite of anticholinergic (which causes mydriasis). Miosis argues against anticholinergic toxidrome and physostigmine.
Q19. A 40-year-old presents after ingesting unknown 'diet pills.' She is confused, has HR 160, temperature 40.5°C, dry skin, and mydriasis. The team is concerned about serotonin syndrome vs. anticholinergic toxidrome. Which finding MOST reliably differentiates anticholinergic from serotonin syndrome?
  • A. Heart rate (both can cause tachycardia)
  • B. Temperature (both can cause hyperthermia)
  • C. Level of consciousness (both can cause delirium)
  • D. Neuromuscular findings: clonus and hyperreflexia present in serotonin syndrome, absent in anticholinergic
❌ Incorrect. Both toxidromes cause tachycardia. Heart rate does not reliably differentiate them.
❌ Incorrect. Both can cause severe hyperthermia. Temperature alone does not differentiate.
❌ Incorrect. Both toxidromes can present with agitation and delirium. Mental status does not reliably differentiate.
✅ Correct. Clonus, hyperreflexia, and myoclonus are hallmarks of serotonin syndrome (from spinal 5-HT2A receptor activation). These findings are absent in anticholinergic toxidrome. This is the most specific distinguishing examination finding.
Q20. Emergency medical technicians bring in a patient from a psychiatric facility who was given intramuscular droperidol and subsequently developed agitation, confusion, hot dry skin, and HR 145. The psychiatric nurse reports the patient 'seemed anticholinergic.' What is the most appropriate disposition for this patient?
  • A. Return to the psychiatric facility with instructions to observe for 4 hours
  • B. Immediate discharge home if ECG shows normal QRS
  • C. Emergency department evaluation with ECG, cardiac monitoring, and treatment of anticholinergic toxidrome
  • D. Direct ICU admission for intubation prophylaxis
❌ Incorrect. HR 145 and anticholinergic delirium require ED evaluation, not return to a facility without monitoring capabilities for acute toxicologic emergencies.
❌ Incorrect. Normal QRS does not mean the patient is safe for immediate discharge. The presentation requires monitoring and treatment.
✅ Correct. The patient needs ED evaluation: ECG (droperidol/antipsychotic exposure warrants QTc assessment), cardiac monitoring, treatment of hyperthermia and agitation, and observation for progression.
❌ Incorrect. Prophylactic intubation is not indicated in an alert patient who can protect their airway. Appropriate monitoring and treatment without automatic intubation is the correct approach.
